routes: POST /api/rating retains its canonical route; no route or response shape change.
apiContracts: Rating writes accept only positive safe-integer novel IDs and whole-number ratings from 1 through 10.
Fractional, non-finite, string-typed, missing, null, out-of-range and unsafe integer inputs are rejected with HTTP 400.
The server does not round or coerce a fractional rating into an accepted value.
dataEntities: ratings; the existing table is upgraded in place from whole-number 1–5 scores to whole-number 1–10 scores, preserving historical values as equivalent even scores.

migrationPlan.canonicalEntityReuse: Migration 0035 rebuilds the existing ratings table with a strict integer 1–10 CHECK constraint; historical integer values 1–5 are mapped to 2,4,6,8,10 and existing timestamps are preserved.
migrationPlan.backwardCompatibility: The API/UI must not deploy before migration 0035. Fresh installs apply baseline 0034 then migration 0035; existing installs convert the existing ratings table. The migration is forward-only.
migrationPlan.rollbackOrForwardRepair: Do not roll back to a 1–5 schema after new odd 1–10 scores have been accepted. Before deployment retain a verified D1 export. If migration fails before Worker rollout, stop deployment and reconcile from the backup or apply a reviewed forward repair. Once new-scale votes exist, use forward repair rather than lossy reverse conversion.

privacySecurity.authorization: Only the authenticated user can write their own rating.
privacySecurity.ownerScoping: Rating writes continue to bind user_id to authenticated session user.
privacySecurity.csrf: Existing write-route CSRF protections remain unchanged.
privacySecurity.rateAndSizeLimits: Existing request body and route limits remain unchanged.
privacySecurity.referentialIntegrity: Existing novel publication and rights-eligibility checks remain unchanged.

unit: test-rating-input-validation.mjs: accepts whole-number 1–10 only; rejects fractions, NaN, Infinity, strings, null, out-of-range values and invalid novel IDs
test-rating-handler-canonical.mjs: assert unique GET/POST handlers, publication and rights gates, 1–10 bounds and no rounding
test-rating-migration.py: fresh install, existing 1–5 conversion, timestamp preservation, aggregate recalculation, rejection of fractional and out-of-range scores.
integration: Mandatory npm build executes rating input regression against the canonical Worker source.
Release gate verifies backup and migration 0035 sequencing before Worker rollout; no 1–10 UI/API deployment is permitted against a legacy schema.
isolation: No ownership or session boundary changes.

stagingSteps: Export and retain a verified D1 backup before schema mutation.
Apply migration 0035 exactly once after confirming the expected legacy/fresh schema.
Verify integer-only 1–10 constraint, preserved vote count/timestamps and recalculated aggregates before Worker deployment.
Run the mandatory build and Cloudflare Source Validation on the exact PR head.
Confirm route registry and API/authorization source fingerprints match the Worker snapshot.

rollback.codeRollback: Revert the route-only validation simplification and regression test if unexpected behavior appears.
rollback.dataRollbackOrForwardRepair: Migration 0035 is forward-only. Keep the pre-migration D1 export; never reverse-scale odd 1–10 ratings after new-scale writes exist. Use a reviewed forward repair for post-rollout defects.
monitoringSignals: HTTP 400 rates for invalid rating submissions

collisionReview.duplicateRoutes: No route added; existing POST /api/rating is updated in place.
collisionReview.duplicateEntities: No new table or data entity.
collisionReview.migrationAllocation: Migration 0035 is reserved in migrations/.reservations/0035.json for PR #195; no competing migration number may be allocated.
collisionReview.sharedSurfaceOwners: Worker route owned by platform-kernel; regression test by platform-quality; package script by repository-operations; contract and ADR by platform-architecture.; migration SQL/reservation owned by platform-data.

changeSummary: Removes redundant Math.round from rating input handling after explicit safe-integer validation, making the 1–10 whole-number contract direct and regression-tested.
acceptanceCriteria: Only positive safe-integer novel IDs are accepted.
No rounding or fractional coercion occurs.
Published and rights-eligible novel checks remain unchanged.
No migration, route addition, response-shape change or browser bundle change.
Migration 0035 upgrades fresh and existing databases to a whole-number 1–10 ratings constraint.
Fractional ratings are rejected by the database, not merely the API.
Migration 0035 is reserved once and release sequencing retains a pre-migration backup.
